hci_traces.host_initiated_wifi_2_4GHz: Connect Request received and accepted (paging works); SSP IO capability exchange with MITM-required dedicated bonding; the phone's scripted NoInputNoOutput agent never answered the numeric comparison, so the host ended the link after 24 s (0x13). Earlier ConnectionAttemptFailed and missed inquiries are intermittent.
hci_traces.phone_initiated_wifi_2_4GHz: Link key notification, encryption on, 16-byte key; SDP exchanged
hci_traces.bonded_rfcomm_wifi_2_4GHz: authentication with stored key and encryption succeed, about 20 KB transferred, then Disconnect Complete: Connection Timeout (0x08), i.e. link supervision timeout
hci_traces.wifi_radio_off: every phone Create Connection fails with Connection Accept Timeout Exceeded (0x10); no pairing
hci_traces.wifi_on_5GHz_ch36: host inquiry never finds the phone in 45 s; phone connections time out; no pairing

interpretation: Two distinct defects. (1) With the WLAN radio off, the Iris PA and RFA/digital rails are off, so Bluetooth has no RF power. Something must keep Iris powered while Bluetooth is in use. (2) With WLAN on 5 GHz the rails stay on but Bluetooth cannot inquire or page, which points to RF-path/coexistence configuration. Prima sends a BTC configuration (WDA_BTC_SET_CFG, execution mode default 0); wcn36xx sends only BTC CFG timing items and no BTC configuration message.
stock_reference: Stock WCNSS_qcom_cfg.ini sets no BTC overrides, so firmware defaults from WCNSS_cfg.dat (extracted privately) applied; wcn36xx sends its own BTC CFG table. Comparing the two is the next step.

iris_rails_by_wlan_state.note: PMIC SPMI readback; Linux drops its Iris votes after WCNSS handover (by design), so the RF supplies follow the Pronto firmware's WLAN-side votes
